# Lab 2: RStudio Projects and Quarto Documents ## Learning Objectives * Create an **RStudio Project** to organize your work. * Understand the structure of a **Quarto (.qmd)** document. * "Render" a document into a professional HTML report. --- ## Part 1: RStudio Projects In Data Science, organization is everything. An RStudio Project keeps your code, data, and images in one "folder" so R always knows where to look. ::: {.callout-important} ## 📝 Lab Task 1: Setting Up Your Workspace Before writing any code, you must organize your environment. Follow these steps to create your project structure: ### Step 1: Create the RStudio Project 1. Open **RStudio**. 2. In the top menu, click **File > New Project…** 3. Select **New Directory** > **New Project**. 4. **Directory Name:** Type `MAT186_Labs`. 5. **Create project as subdirectory of:** Click *Browse* and select your **Documents** folder. 6. Click **Create Project**. ### Step 2: Create Professional Sub-folders Data scientists never leave files "floating" in the main folder. Use the **Files pane** (bottom-right window) to create a professional structure: 1. Click the **New Folder** button. 2. Type `data` and click **OK**. (This is where you will save datasets). 3. Click the **New Folder** button again. 4. Type `images` and click **OK**. (This is where you will save plots and graphs). ::: ::: {.callout-note} ### Why do this? By creating these now, you are ready for Lab 5! You will put all your datasets in `/data` and all your plots/diagrams in `/images`. ::: --- ## Part 2: Creating a Quarto Document # Lab 2: Introduction to Quarto Quarto allows you to combine text, code, and results into one professional document. Follow these steps to get started. ## Creating your Document 1. In the top menu, click **File > New File > Quarto Document...** 2. Title it **"Lab 2"** and put your name as the **Author**. 3. Click **Create**. It will open a quarto document. --- ## The Three Parts of a Quarto Document A Quarto document is made of three distinct components: ### 1. The YAML Header Look at the very top of the file. You will see text between two sets of three dashes (`---`). This is the **YAML Header**; it contains the "metadata" or settings for your document. ```yaml --- title: "Lab 2" author: "Your Name" format: html editor: visual --- ``` ### 2. Markdown (Narrative) The plain white areas of the document are called **Markdown**. This is where you write your analysis, explain your results, and answer questions. It works like a simplified word processor. * You can make text **bold** by using `**double asterisks**`. * You can make text *italic* by using `*single asterisks*`. ### 3. Code Chunks The gray boxes starting with ` ```{r} ` and ending with ` ``` ` are called **Code Chunks**. This is where you put your R code to run calculations or create graphs. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # This is a code chunk. R code goes here! 1 + 1 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 2 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note} ## Tip for Students To run the code inside a chunk, click the green **Play** button in the top-right corner of the gray box. The result will appear directly below the chunk! ::: --- ## Part 3: Rendering (The "Magic" Button) To turn your code into a report: 1. Click the **Render** button (blue arrow icon) at the top of the editor. 2. RStudio will save the file and pop up a beautiful HTML window. --- ::: {.callout-important} ## 📝 Lab Task 2: Your First Calculation Follow these steps to practice using Quarto: 1. **Create a Document**: In RStudio, go to **File > New File > Quarto Document**. Name it `Lab2_yourname`. 2. **Clean the Workspace**: Find the heading that says **Quarto**. Delete all the example text and code *below* that line so you have a blank white space. 3. **Add a Title**: In that new blank area, type a title for your work: `# Lab 2`. *(Note: Using the # symbol makes the text large like a heading!)* 4. **Insert a Chunk**: Click the **+C** button to create a new gray R chunk. Inside the chunk, type: `2 + 2` 5. **Render the Report**: Click the **Render** button (blue arrow icon) at the top of your screen. 6. **Check Results**: Look at your final HTML report. You should see your title **Lab 2**, the code `2 + 2`, and the result `4`. 7. **Submit**: upload your HTML report in Brightspace and submit it. ::: --- ::: {.callout-tip} ### Done with the Lab? If you have finished all the tasks above, you can verify your work against the official solutions.
